title: The TE101 resonance of a rectangular cavity
shows: A 100 × 80 × 50 mm box with perfectly conducting walls, driven by a current along its height, resonates in TE101 at (c/2)·√((1/a)² + (1/d)²) = 3.352 GHz. The box is cut into 10 mm cubes, each split into six tetrahedra: long, flat boxes converge far more slowly.
source: Rectangular cavity resonators: D. M. Pozar, Microwave Engineering, 4th ed. (2012), §6.3.
